BASIC ENVIRONMENTAL TESTING PROCEDURES FOR ELECTRO.NIC AND ELECTRICAL ITEMS
PART XVI DRIVING RAIN TEST

0.
0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard ( Part XVI ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 17 February 1983, after the draft finalized by the Environmental Testing Procedures Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council.

0.2 The differences in environmental testing procedures for component type items and equipment type items are fast disappearing in the context of technological developments. It is, therefore, felt necessary to have This series of standards uniform testing procedures wherever possible. on environmental testing procedures ( IS : 9000 ) has been prepared with this objective. This is also in line with the principle adopted by testing ' in developing unified series IEC/TC 50 g Environmental of standards on environmental testing procedures by the International Electrotechnical Commission. 0.2.1 It is proposed to withdraw the existing Indian Standards, namely, IS : 589-1961* and IS : 210St series dealing with environmental tests for electronic components and equipment respectively, as soon as the tests mentioned therein are covered in the new series ( IS : 9000 ). 0.3 While preparing this standard, assistance is derived from JSS 555551977 Environmental test methods for electronic and electrical equipment. Directorate of Standardization, Ministry of Defence, India. 0.4 In reporting the result of a test made in accordance with standard, if the. final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960:. this off,

*Basic climatic and mechanical durability tests for components for electronic and electrical equipment ( revised ). tEnvironmenta1 tests for electronic and electrical equipment.
$Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

1.1 This standard ( Part XVI ) deals with the procedure for application of rain test on electronic and electrical items as a part of the basic environmental testing procedures.
2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions terms given in IS : 9000 ( Part I )-1977* shall apply. 3. OBJECT 3.1 The object of this test is to determine the suitability electrical items for use under conditions of rain, 4. TEST of electronic and and explanation of

4.2 The driving rain chamber shall be capable of spraying water under laboratory atmospheric conditions at a static pressure of 200 kPa f 15 percent from 8 shower heads.

7. CONDITIONING 7.1 The item shall be subjected to this test, in its ` unpacked ' and ` switched-off' condition. Three test conditions are specified for this test. The item shall be subjected to one of the test conditions as specified in 7.1.3. 7.1.1 The item under test, while being under the laboratory conditions shall be suitably positioned inside the chamber in its normal operational attitude as specified. `; 1.2 Tap water at laboratory temperature and at a static pressure of 200 kPa f 15 percent shall be sprayed for 1 hour or any other period as specified in the relevant specification. The consumption of water from each shower head shall be 450 litres ri: 10 percent per hour. 7.1.3 Spray from the shower heads shall be directed as given in one of the three test conditions given below: a) Test condition A - Spray from four shower heads shall be directed at an angle of 45' at each of the four uppermost corners of the item. 7

IS : 9000 ( Part XVI ) - 1983
b) Test condition B - Spray from four shower heads shall be directed horizontally at the centre of each of the four sides of the rquipment.

c) Test condition C - The item shall be sprayed from eight shower heads, four of them being directed at an angle of 4.5" on each of the uppermost corners of the item and the rcnlaining four bein,? directed horizontally at the centre of the area of each of tile four sides of the item. 7.1.4 At the conclusion of the period specified, the item shall he removed from the chamber and, if required by the relevant specification, a performance check shall he carried out. 8. RECOVERY 8.1 Unless otherwise specified, the external surfaces of the item shall dried by wiping or by applying a blast of air at room temperature. 9. FINAL MEASUREMENTS be

9.1 The item shall be examined for undue penetration of water; and shall be visually inspected and electrically and rnecllanically chekccl, as required by the relevant specification. 10. INFORMATION
